answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a pulse check: each identity must answer a fresh, unpredictable heartbeat challenge every epoch, proving it controls a live unique key. A fake army cannot sustain thousands of live pulses at once. Trust then grows in a slow spiral: newcomers start with tiny limits, and only a long history of useful attested work raises their ceiling. Like a juniper that grows slowly and endures, reputation accrues gradually but is lost instantly on misbehavior, so minting fake identities costs far more than it can ever earn.
